summary.text: An 11-hour-old male newborn, born by cesarean section at 38 weeks and 4 days, was transferred to a tertiary hospital with significant respiratory distress. A chest x-ray showed right-sided tension pneumothorax with mediastinal and tracheal shift, and he was diagnosed with meconium aspiration syndrome complicated by bronchopleural fistula.

Several days of positive pressure ventilation brought no significant improvement in pulmonary findings or oxygenation. After discussion with the surgeon, closed chest drainage was implemented and HFOV was started with a 6.5 Fr chest tube. Serial blood gas sets and HFOV adjustments followed, with worsening dyspnea, volume expansion, thoracentesis and closed drainage. Three days after HFOV, frequent desaturation and dyspnea occurred, and repeated chest tube changes further compromised ventilation.

Ventilator parameters were reduced and VA-ECMO was started with lung rest settings. Right pneumothorax improved by the third and fourth days, then worsened on the fifth day after PEEP increases, and a BPF was suspected. Intubation was removed on day 8, restarted ventilation on day 10 aggravated the pneumothorax, and intubation was pulled out again.

Two days later the chest tube showed no gas outflow with no obvious pneumothorax, and ventilator-assisted ventilation was started again. No pneumothorax was seen on chest x-rays at 12 h and 24 h after intubation, suggesting the BPF healed by itself. He was disconnected from ECMO on day 14, extubated to non-invasive support on day 17, and discharged on day 23.

ambiguities.issue: The reference point of the day numbers is not stated; it may count from ECMO initiation or from admission. The bare "On day 8/10/14/17/23" series in the same Case report paragraph uses one day count and orders its own events; "from day 5" (prone ventilation) sits in the earlier paragraph next to "the third/fourth/fifth day after ECMO" and is not shown to share that count, so it is not ordered against either series.

evidence.quote: Intermittent prone position ventilation was performed every 12 h to reduce lung inflammation from day 5.
On day 8, to allow a good rest of the lungs
On day 23, the patient's condition improved, and he was discharged.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not equate "from day 5" with "On the fifth day after ECMO", order it against the day 8 to 23 series or the ECMO-day series, or assign calendar dates to the day numbers.

ambiguities.issue: A bronchopleural fistula is stated as part of the initial diagnosis, but after ECMO and PEEP increases the text says a BPF "was suspected".

evidence.quote: The newborn was diagnosed with meconium aspiration syndrome (MAS), complicated by BPF.
Based on the clinical and radiological findings, a BPF was suspected.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which statement reflects the diagnostic certainty at each time.

ambiguities.issue: The five blood gas sets, the HFOV settings and the dyspnea changes are described in sequence, but only set 5 states a time (1 h after the interventions); the source does not state intervals between the other sets or link each gas set to a named time.

ambiguities.issue: The Discussion says that the patient was treated with VA-ECMO but also describes veno-venous ECMO and "awake ECMO" in general terms, and calls the fistula "BPT" once; these Discussion sentences are not recorded as extra patient facts.

we chose VA-ECMO as our first option

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not add VV-ECMO or tracheostomy to this patient.

ambiguities.issue: The Discussion states "Later, when we lowered PEEP, the pneumothorax improved", but the Case report never describes a PEEP reduction; it describes extubation on day 8.

ambiguities.issue: The Introduction and abstract call the pneumothorax spontaneous, whereas the Case report diagnoses meconium aspiration syndrome complicated by BPF and attributes persistence of the BPF to positive pressure ventilation.
